summary: Ephemeral runner sessions staleness and credential reuse observed during bulk Vault rewrap
description: Issue summary: During a scheduled mass rewrap of Transit keys in Vault (part of the quarterly secret rotation), a subset of ephemeral GitHub Actions runners began reusing stale runner session tokens for new jobs. Impact: ~12% of release pipeline jobs failed to start or timed out (job hang), causing release windows to slip for two services and increasing CI queue times. Hypothesis: race between token rewrap and runner bootstrap leading to cached token reuse and transient auth failures. We believe a TTL/grace mismatch and a non-atomic update in the runner agent's credential refresh logic exposed this during the high-concurrency rotation window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger bulk Vault Transit rewrap in prod-us-east (simulate using rotation job in infra-tools).
2) Immediately trigger parallel release pipelines that provision ephemeral runners (50+ simultaneous jobs).
3) Observe runner bootstrap logs for token fetch attempts and any token cache hits prior to successful renewals.
4) Monitor CI controller for job-assignment failures and GitHub Actions runner heartbeats.
observed_behavior: Runners reported authentication success to controller but then failed when fetching job payloads (403/401) or stalled for >3 minutes waiting on agent start. Some agents reported using a cached token that no longer matched Vault's wrapped ciphertext post-rewrap.

investigation_notes: Checked Vault rotation timeline: transit rewrap started 02:13:54Z and completed 02:15:00Z for primary keyset.
Observed increased runner bootstrap concurrency at 02:14:05-02:14:30Z correlated with rotation window.
Agent code path: credential manager has a short TTL caching layer (configurable) that does not validate wrap_id after rewrap -> potential stale token reuse.
No KMS downtime; observed no errors on backend Vault cluster. The issue reproduces reliably with synthetic load (50+ parallel ephemeral runners) and a fast rewrap job.
Workaround tested: temporarily increase token-grace TTL on runner agent and stagger rotation; reduced failure rate to <1% in canary tests.
Related infra alert: vault-transit-high-latency (A-7892) fired during the window but resolved automatically.

Marco Ruiz (2026-03-09): Investigating runner agent credential cache; adding a trace build to surface wrap_id on cached entries. Assigning to SRE for Vault timeline verification.
SRE - Priya Menon (2026-03-10): Vault rewrap completed cleanly; no cluster errors. Reproduced failure in staging with parallel job load and fast rewrap. Likely an agent race.
Release Eng - Daniel Cho (2026-03-11): Deployed temporary stagger for rotations and extended token-grace to 120s. Immediate releases resumed; still need a proper code fix in agent.
planned_resolution: Short term: coordinate staggered rotation windows and increase agent token-grace TTL to 120s for next scheduled rotation; patch release to update agent to validate wrap_id before reusing cached credentials. Long term: implement atomic rotate-and-notify pattern in infra-tools so agents can invalidate cache via push event during rewrap. Backport fix to release runners and schedule controlled canary in staging before wider rollout. Postmortem and runbook update assigned to Marco Ruiz and Priya Menon.
